records.quote: 4. Allow the droplet to stabilize in the microgravity environment.
records.derivation: Step 4 of the list introduced by 'The overall investigation approach can be summarized as:' in the same field; it places the deployed test droplet in the microgravity environment. No g-level stated. Not used: section=projectType 'Microgravity Investigation' (category label) and the SRD 5.1.7 acceleration requirement (pages 39 and 44, a pre-flight requirement, not a reported condition).

records.quote: By conducting these experiments in a microgravity environment, the effects of buoyancy are minimized, and the droplet can be characterized only as a function of thermocapillary or solutalcapillary stresses allowing for a clear observation of the fundamental combustion processes,  The present FLEX-2 experiments using bi-component mixtures.
records.derivation: The sentence sits in the PSI 'hypothesis' field and gives the rationale for microgravity, so it is proposed as ambiguous (brief rule 3). The double space after 'processes,' and the run-on ending are as written in the record.

records.quote: Fuel purity: Purity levels shall be the highest purity level that is commercially available (research grade at 99.5% by volume at present) and all liquids shall be degassed and contain no H2O.
records.derivation: Paragraph under '5.1.1 Test Fuels' (printed page 33); 'all liquids' are the test fuels (pure fuels and binary mixtures). The sentence spans three PDF lines, joined with single spaces; 'H2O' has a subscript 2 in the PDF. The SRD is the pre-flight requirements document dated March 15, 2010 (page 1).

records.quote: While FLEX is focussed on spacecraft fire safety and fire suppression, FLEX-2 returns to the broader objective of improving the [...] understanding of liquid-fuel combustion.
records.derivation: Introduction, printed page 1. '[...]' skips only the word 'fundamental', which is hyphenated across a PDF line break ('fun-' / 'damental'); the other line break ('spacecraft' / 'fire') is joined with one space. Names the phase of the fuels FLEX-2 studies as a whole.

records.quote: FLEX-2 (The Flame Extinguishment - 2) experiment is the second experiment to fly on the ISS which uses small droplets of fuel to study the special spherical characteristics of burning fuel droplets in space.
records.derivation: The sentence says 'droplets of fuel' but does not name the phase; liquid inferred from the droplet form.

PSI flight-program field (the whole field). Consistent with R7 (DoD) and with SRD page 29: 'The flight experiment utilizes the Multiple Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) installed in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) in the International Space Station (ISS) to investigate several fundamental aspects of droplet combustion.'

records.quote: FLEX-2 (The Flame Extinguishment - 2) experiment is the second experiment to fly on the ISS which uses small droplets of fuel to study the special spherical characteristics of burning fuel droplets in space.
records.derivation: Source writes only the acronym 'ISS'; value uses the full name written in section=flightProgram (R6). 'in space' in this sentence was not used for gravity_regime.

records.quote: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)
records.derivation: The field lists two items; this record takes the first. Shared with FLEX per SRD page 7 (see lineage).

records.quote: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Multi-user Droplet Combustion Appartatus (MDCA)
records.derivation: Second item of the field; 'Appartatus' is spelled this way in the PSI record (sic). The MDCA is an apparatus inside the CIR; proposed as platform so the auditor can accept or reject it. Naming variant: SRD page 29 expands the acronym as 'Multiple Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)', SRD page 7 as 'multiuser droplet combustion apparatus, MDCA'. Same acronym and rack, so DISCREPANCY not raised. Shared with FLEX per SRD page 7 (see lineage).

records.quote: The investigation has 40 Experiment Data records which are based on the Test Matrix (Binary Array, Condensed Phase, LCTFCalibration, LCTFWavelengths, Quiescent, RadiometerCalibration, SurrotgateFuel), Fuel Composition, and/or Year.
records.derivation: 'Quiescent' is one of the Test Matrix names under which PSI groups the Experiment Data records; that its tests had no imposed flow is inferred from the label, the sentence does not describe the flow. test_id is the Test Matrix name as written.

records.test_id: single-droplet tests other than the convective flow tests
records.quote: The ignited droplets burns to either completion or the flame extinguishes at a finite droplet radius in a quiescent ambient.
records.derivation: Pre-flight SRD (printed page 25) describing the planned generic single-droplet test. In the same paragraph the convective flow tests impose a flow (R12) and the array tests have no flow condition stated, so the sentence does not cover every test; the SRD gives no PSI test ids, so test_id describes the scope in words. The sentence spans two PDF lines ('finite' / 'droplet'), joined with one space; 'droplets burns' is as written.

records.quote: In the convective flow tests the droplet is subjected to a known and controlled small, sub-buoyant flow.
records.derivation: None of the controlled terms (opposed, concurrent, quiescent, coflow) fits, so the term is kept as written. SRD page 42 (5.1.5) says the flow field may be established by translating a tethered droplet; record section=approach says 'If the flow field is to be generated by translating the droplet then droplet motion would commence at the same time that the ignitor is retracted.' The SRD is pre-flight, and the DoD Test Matrix list (paragraph 1) names no convective or translation matrix. The sentence spans two PDF lines ('a' / 'known'), joined with one space.

not_found.variable: gravity_regime = normal_gravity (1-g comparison tests run by this investigation)
not_found.looked_in: Record text, all sections; DoD paragraphs 1-7; SRD pages 1-68. None found. SRD page 27, Figure 11 ('Burning of ethanol droplet in normal-gravity under 1 and 2 atmospheric pressures.') is an unattributed background image in Research Goals, not tied to any FLEX-2 test. The SRD 7.1 ground experiments (page 56) are drop-tower microgravity rigs, not PSI flight data.

not_found.variable: flow_configuration for the Binary Array tests
not_found.looked_in: SRD page 31 describes the array tests ('two droplets are placed along a support fiber at known locations and the droplets are ignited simultaneously') without a flow condition; SRD pages 20-23, 28 and 40-41 (arrays background, research goal, pinning-bead spacing; PDF page indices) do not state one either; record text and DoD silent.

not_found.variable: flow_configuration (post-flight statement that convective or translated-droplet tests were run)
not_found.looked_in: Record section=approach gives only a conditional sentence ('If the flow field is to be generated by translating the droplet...') and lists 'Droplet translation velocity (and acceleration)' among the independently varied parameters; DoD paragraph 1 Test Matrix list has no convective matrix; the SRD (2010) states plans only.

lineage: FLEX-2 runs in the MDCA inside the CIR on the ISS, the same apparatus and rack the SRD says FLEX (FLEX-1) was designed for. SRD page 7: 'the Flammability-limit experiment FLEX, was designed for the International Space Station, ISS, to be run using the multiuser droplet combustion [...] MDCA, in the combustion integrated rack, CIR.' ('[...]' skips 'apparatus,', hyphenated across a line break.) The SRD also reuses DCE-1 OH* imaging (page 48) and FLEX support-fiber limits (page 40).
